Subject: Rerank/classifier pricing question — how is scoring billed?

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — the reranker looked promising. Before we move further in procurement, finance needs clarity on how Redwood bills scoring for rerank/classifier endpoints. A few concrete questions:

- Do you bill per API call (per request) or per candidate scored (e.g., if we send 1 request with 10 candidates, is that 1 unit or 10 units)?
- If we use a batch endpoint that returns top-k with scores, is that billed differently than calling a scoring-only endpoint for each candidate?
- Are there minimums or rounding rules (e.g., partial candidate rounding, min charge per request)?

For context — our expected profile is ~10M request events/day where each event is a short query with an average of 5 candidates (we sometimes run top-k retrieval upstream and send ~20 candidates in experiments). We will be on hosted API (no dedicated commit initially).

Can you share a baseline rate card and an example cost calc for our volume? Also interested in any volume/tier discounts or packaging that avoids unpredictable spikes (we have seasonal bursts).

Appreciate a short written breakdown we can share with procurement.

Best,
Samantha

Acme Analytics

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rerank/classifier pricing question — how is scoring billed?

Samantha — thanks for the clear questions and the volume detail, that helps a lot. Summary up front: for our hosted API we bill rerank/classifier scoring on a per-candidate (per-score) basis, not per-request. That means if you send one API request with 10 candidates and we score all 10, that's billed as 10 scoring units. A few elaborations below and a sample calc attached.

Key points:
- Billing unit: "score" — every distinct candidate we score (including candidates we return). If the model computes a score for a candidate, it counts as one scored item.
- Batch vs single-call: batching does not give you a free multiplicative discount — billing is still per scored candidate. Batching reduces latency and throughput overhead, but we charge on scoring units, not HTTP calls.
- Top-k returned vs scored-offline: if you request top-3 but the system scores 10 candidates to pick top-3, you are billed for 10 scores. If you use a specialized endpoint that only scores the returned items and does less work, we'd bill accordingly; we can instrument that in the ratecard note.
- Rounding/minimums: smallest billing unit is 1 scored candidate. There is no sub-candidate rounding. We surface per-day aggregated counts for billing and round to the nearest whole scored unit.
- Token-based components: for classifier models that rely on tokenized input (e.g., text segments), there can also be a small token-based component in addition to per-score if the call triggers text-generation or heavier pre/post-processing; we'll call that out per-model.

Attached: ACME_RateCard_v2.pdf (baseline unit prices and tier structure) and scoring_pricing_calculator.xlsx (example math for your 10M events/day profile).

Example cost sketch (hosted, no commit):
- Baseline price: $0.0006 per scored candidate (example, see attached for model-specific tiers).
- Your baseline: 10M events/day * 5 candidates = 50M scored candidates/day.
- Daily: 50M * $0.0006 = $30,000/day (~$900k/month) — this is illustrative; actual per-model price varies and we have tiered discounts.

Discount/packaging options to reduce volatility:
1) Tiered automatic discounts — price per score steps down as lifetime monthly volume hits thresholds (in attachment).
2) Committed monthly spend (Reserved/Dedicated) — 12m commit gives up to 25% discount and predictable unit pricing; also gives you access to burst capacity and SLA.
3) Pre-purchased scoring credits — good for procurement who want to purchase a pooled credit bucket at a negotiated rate.
4) Throttle policies & cost controls — you can set per-route caps via the Console to limit spend from sudden spikes.

If helpful, we can produce an alternate calc that assumes an average of 20 candidates for A/B experiments (the attached sheet has toggles). Also looping in Laura (acct lead) and Neha (SE) to help scope model selection (since model choice impacts per-score price).

Would you like a short 30-minute call with finance + SE to get a committed package quote and walk the calculator?

Samantha — great questions, answered inline below and with next steps.

- "Scored-returned-only" mode: we do offer a specialized mode for some model/endpoint combos that only computes scores for the items explicitly requested to be scored (e.g., you can call a top-k-only scoring mode). Availability depends on model and objective — Neha can validate which model options support it. If the endpoint does less internal work (fewer scored candidates) we'll bill fewer scoring units.

- Aggregation & rounding: billing aggregates scored units per calendar day per account. We sum all scored candidates and bill the total; there is no per-request rounding. That means running 1 request for 3 candidates and 1 for 2 candidates yields 5 scored units that day — no per-call rounding surprises. The only rounding is at the unit level: fractional internal instrumentations are rounded to whole scored units before aggregation.

- Latency (P50/P95): on hosted multi-tenant with our optimized reranker model we typically see P50 ~ 28–40ms and P95 ~ 120–180ms for single-request scoring of 5–10 candidates on standard routes. If you plan 50M scored candidates/day we recommend a committed package (Dedicated) to get predictable P95 SLOs and capacity guarantees — Neha can scope expected concurrency needs based on your QPS.

- Taxes/VAT: for hosted usage we invoice net of local taxes; Redwood will include applicable VAT/SST on the invoice where required per your billing address and local regs. If you have a reseller agreement, please loop them in and Ops can coordinate tax handling. Rishi (cc'd) can provide the standard tax language for the MSA.
